transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Owen Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Torres (BlueApollo Head of ML), Raj Singh (Platform Eng), Emily Park (Security)

Auto-summary: quick sign-off on success criteria and acceptance tests, define benchmark scope and reporting. Action items assigned for SOW, benchmark harness, test data and security confirmation.

00:00 Lena: okay hi everyone sorry for slight delay, we had a brief infra meeting, thanks for squeezing us in
00:08 Maya: no problem lena, great to see you, this is maya from redwood inference, i'll run through the agenda quick and then owen will take the benchmarks/tech details
00:18 Owen: hi all, nice to meet you, um so high level today's goal is to get explicit success criteria and acceptance tests for the POC so both sides have go/no-go thresholds and reporting format
00:30 Raj: sounds good, our timeline is tight, we want results in two weeks ideally so we can decide by end of october for a pilot
00:40 Maya: yep totally, we captured earlier you wanted latency and cost per request to be comparable to your current endpoint, and model output quality to match or exceed your current vendor. today we want to make those explicit
00:55 Lena: okay i'm going to be blunt, we need: 1) latency p95 under 300ms for 1k token prompts, 2) throughput >= 200 reqs/min sustained for our peak, 3) semantic fidelity measured by human eval on 300 samples with pass rate > 90% for top-tier prompts, 4) cost per 1k tokens <= $0.12 equivalent. those are our acceptance thresholds, but we can be flexible if the reporting and degradation behavior is clear
01:20 Owen: nice, that's concrete which helps. couple clarifying q's: when you say 1k token prompts is that worst-case, or average? and the 200 reqs/min is parallel requests or sequential?
01:34 Lena: it's worst-case single request with long context, avg is around 600 tokens. 200 reqs/min is sustained concurrent throughput across a single dedicated cluster — we can specify exact qps shape later
01:46 Owen: got it. for the POC we'll run two benchmark profiles: A) worst-case long-context latency (1k tokens), B) realistic mixed profile (60/30/10 split short/medium/long) to measure cost and tail. we'll also run a quality eval with your 300-sample set and an additional 200 randomized cases
02:05 Raj: ok on the env: we'll provide a private S3 bucket with redacted test data and IAM token, we expect the POC to run in Redwood Dedicated or Private mode depending on your recommended setup — is there a preference?
02:18 Owen: for initial benchmarks we recommend Dedicated (reserved pool) to get stable latency; we can demonstrate hosted later. Dedicated will give predictable throughput and easier debugging of tail latency. for the POC report we'll include both latency distribution and cost model extrapolated to your traffic
02:33 Emily: from security side we need KEK/KMS integration details, audit logs, and data retention/capture policy. SOC2 docs would help, also any redwood private deployment checklist
02:45 Maya: absolutely we will share SOC2 attestation and the private deployment checklist. for KMS we support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS) and HSM integrations — we'll include the integration guide
02:55 Lena: ok good. about acceptance tests, we want pass/fail criteria that are deterministic where possible. for example: if p95 latency <= 300ms AND semantic pass rate >= 90% on the 300-sample set, then POC = pass. if one fails but the others meet, we'll classify as partial pass and decide on mitigations
03:20 Owen: proposed acceptance matrix:
- Latency: p95 <= 300ms for 1k context (measured over 30-minute steady-state run)
- Throughput: sustained >= 200 reqs/min for 10 minute window with <1% error rate
- Quality: human eval pass >= 90% on control set of 300 prompts; automatic reranking metrics (if used) to be within 5% of your baseline
- Cost: extrapolated cost per 1k tokens <= $0.12 under your live traffic mix (we'll provide spreadsheet calculation)
- Security: KMS + audit log integration verified, and data residency in us-east-1 for POC

03:55 Lena: that matrix looks reasonable, couple items: can we make the quality test reproducible? we want to ensure inter-annotator agreement and the exact rubric
04:05 Owen: yes we'll include the rubric and a sample annotation sheet. we'll also run a small blinded eval where your annotators don't know which vendor produced which output to reduce bias
04:16 Raj: on workload sizing, our daily peak is 1.2M tokens/hour, typical concurrency at peak is 80 concurrent requests, average request 600 tokens. we need the benchmark to simulate weekend and weekday peak shapes
04:30 Owen: good numbers, we'll configure the harness to replay traffic shape and synthetic spikes. for throughput thresholds we'll test sustained and spike recovery times (time to 95% of throughput after a spike)
04:40 Maya: about reporting format — we propose a POC report pdf + CSV raw results + an interactive dashboard link (temporary console) summarizing p50/p95/p99 latencies, token costs, error logs, and the human eval summary including per-prompt pass/fail and annotator comments
04:58 Lena: CSV and dashboard is fine, but we need a short executive one-pager that states go/no-go in plain terms for the leadership review
05:07 Maya: yes we'll produce a 1-page executive summary with final recommendation and whether POC passed defined acceptance criteria
05:12 Emily: security sign-off needs: network diagram, KMS flow, list of retained logs and retention periods, and proof that no customer data persists beyond retention window
05:23 Owen: we'll add those sections to the security appendix of the report and include log retention configs. for the POC we can sign an addendum to the NDA specifying ephemeral data handling if needed
05:35 Raj: about the test environment — will you need a VPC peering or can we provide a temporary VPC endpoint? cost/ops prefer not to open wide peering unless required
05:47 Owen: we can do VPC endpoint/private link into Redwood Dedicated; we'll provide step-by-step network setup. we can also run initial tests over a secure tunnel if that's simpler for ops team
05:58 Lena: timeline recap? you said benchmarks week of 10/20, we have a milestone review 10/31, so we need the final report by 10/27 ideally
06:08 Maya: timeline we propose: 10/16 - Redwood receives test data + credentials; 10/17 - Redwood sends final SOW + pricing; 10/20-10/24 - run benchmark profiles; 10/25 - internal QA and human eval; 10/27 - deliver final report; 10/31 - decision meeting. sound right?
06:28 Lena: yes that aligns. please make the 10/16 and 10/17 dates firm in the SOW
06:33 Owen: quick note on measurement noise: we'll capture at least three runs for each profile and report mean and stddev; acceptance uses the median run but we will highlight best/worst cases
06:44 Raj: how do you calculate extrapolated cost? we want the formula and the assumptions in spreadsheet form so we can validate
06:51 Maya: we'll attach a cost model spreadsheet with assumptions: tokenization rules, batching efficiency, GPU-hour costs, throughput curves. we'll also show sensitivity analysis for +/-20% traffic variance
07:02 Lena: great. any blockers from security or platform?
07:06 Emily: KMS and retention items look reasonable in principle, but we need the SOC2 docs and the integration guide before we approve network access. i'll review the draft when you send it
07:15 Maya: will do, expect SOC2 + integration guide in the SOW bundle; owen will include the benchmark harness and sample commands
07:22 Owen: for acceptance tests, we will publish an automated report template where each test has: test id, description, raw values, pass/fail, notes. we'll sync on the exact CSV columns now: test_id, profile, metric, value, threshold, pass_fail, notes, run_timestamp. any other fields?
07:40 Lena: include a column for anonymized prompt id and annotator id for the human eval section, and a free text notes column for root cause on any fails
07:50 Owen: noted. also we'll surface request/response samples for failed prompts with redaction markers only, not full PII
08:00 Maya: ok to recap next steps: maya to send SOW + pricing by 10/17, owen to deliver benchmark harness and test script by 10/19, raj to provide data link by 10/16, emily to confirm KMS requirements by 10/16, schedule benchmark run for 10/20-10/24, deliver report by 10/27
08:20 Lena: that matches our expectations. one more ask — if POC is a partial pass, can you provide a remediation plan including an estimated engineering delta and timeline?
08:31 Owen: yes we'll include remediation options ranked by effort and expected latency/cost impact; e.g., model quantization, batching tuning, KV cache policies, or Dedicated cluster resizing
08:42 Maya: and we'll include clear acceptance gating for a partial pass (e.g., if latency misses but quality meets, outline temporary scaling/fallback plan)
08:50 Raj: fine by us. any competitors we should be aware of? we've been testing a few, anthro.. anthropic and openai for hosted and a cohere eval, this POC is to evaluate long-term cost/latency tradeoffs
08:59 Maya: understood. okay if there are no further questions i'd like a verbal sign-off on the acceptance matrix now so we can bake it into the SOW
09:07 Lena: verbally sign-off from blueapollo: latency p95 <= 300ms, throughput >= 200 reqs/min, quality human pass >= 90% on 300-sample set, cost <= $0.12 per 1k tokens, security checks in place — pending SOC2 docs. sign-off subject to receiving SOW and test plan
09:28 Maya: great, recording that as formal sign-off subject to SOW. we'll follow up with the SOW and schedule. thanks everyone
09:36 Raj: thanks all, talk soon
09:40 Meeting ends

References shared: POC SOW template (link: https://redwood.example.com/sow/POC-template), benchmark spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/BAA-cost-model.csv), security deck (link: https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2-deck.pdf)

Action items (auto): Maya to send SOW + price; Owen to deliver harness and scripts; Raj to share data; Emily to confirm KMS details.
